lead: An optical fibre is classified by how its refractive index changes across the core and by how many light paths it can carry. A step-index fibre changes index abruptly at the core–cladding boundary. A graded-index fibre changes it smoothly, so rays bend inside the core. A single-mode fibre has a tiny core and carries one mode; a multimode fibre has a wider core and carries many. These choices set dispersion and bandwidth in links such as campus networks and cable TV. Only a few universities teach this classification in detail.
prereq: You need: 5.7 core, cladding and numerical aperture.

blocks.text: In a step-index fibre the core has refractive index n<sub>1</sub> and the cladding has lower index n<sub>2</sub>. The change at core radius a is abrupt. Light is guided by total internal reflection at this boundary. A wide core allows many ray angles, called modes. Different modes take different path lengths, so they arrive at different times. This spreading is modal dispersion; it limits the bit rate.

A graded-index fibre has no sharp jump. Its index is highest on the axis and falls smoothly to n<sub>2</sub> at radius a. A ray away from the axis bends back through lower-index glass, so its path curves. A longer curved path lies mostly in lower-index glass, where light travels faster. Arrival times become closer and modal dispersion falls. The profile is harder to manufacture.

sections.h3: Single-mode, multimode and the V number

blocks.text: Core size sets the mode count. A single-mode fibre has a core of a few micrometres. It carries one mode, has almost no modal dispersion, and gives high bandwidth over long links. A multimode fibre has a core of tens of micrometres. It carries many modes and is easier to connect, but modal dispersion limits its reach. Attenuation and link design are in 5.9.

blocks.where: V is the normalized frequency; a is core radius in μm; λ is vacuum wavelength in μm; n<sub>1</sub> is core index; n<sub>2</sub> is cladding index. NA = √(n<sub>1</sub>² − n<sub>2</sub>²). Single mode needs V < 2.405. For step-index multimode, M ≈ V²/2, where M is the approximate mode count.

blocks.text: Using diameter instead of radius in V doubles V and multiplies M by four. A graded-index multimode fibre may need a different mode-count formula, but V < 2.405 is still the single-mode test.

figure.caption: Refractive index against radius for the example: step-index jumps at 25 μm; graded-index falls smoothly from 1.48 to 1.46. The 50 μm diameter gives a = 25 μm for V.

spec.aria: A graph of refractive index n against radius r in micrometres. The step-index curve is flat at 1.48 up to 25 micrometres, then drops abruptly to 1.46; the graded-index curve falls smoothly from 1.48 at the centre to 1.46 at 25 micrometres and stays at 1.46.

examples.question: A step-index fibre has core diameter 50 μm, n<sub>1</sub> = 1.48, n<sub>2</sub> = 1.46 and operates at λ = 1.30 μm. Find the numerical aperture, V number and approximate number of modes.
steps: V > 2.405, so the fibre is multimode.
examples.answer: NA = 0.2425, V = 29.3, and M ≈ 429 modes; the fibre is multimode.
examples.check:
import math
d = 50.0
a = d / 2
n1 = 1.48
n2 = 1.46
lam = 1.30
NA = math.sqrt(n1**2 - n2**2)
V = (2 * math.pi * a / lam) * NA
M = V**2 / 2
print(f"{NA:.4f}")
print(f"{V:.1f}")
print(f"{M:.0f}")

traps: Use core radius, not diameter, in V. Using diameter doubles V and makes M four times too large.
V < 2.405 means single mode, not many modes.
A large NA collects more light but can increase modal dispersion in a multimode step-index fibre.
A graded-index fibre is not automatically single-mode; it is single-mode only if V < 2.405.

quiz.q: State the difference between step-index and graded-index refractive-index profiles.
quiz.a: Step-index changes n abruptly at the core edge; graded-index changes it smoothly from centre to edge.

quiz.q: Why does a single-mode fibre have high bandwidth?
quiz.a: It supports one mode, so modal dispersion is almost absent.

quiz.q: A fibre has a = 5 μm, n<sub>1</sub> = 1.45, n<sub>2</sub> = 1.44, λ = 1.30 μm. Find V and the mode type.
A step-index fibre has V = 20. Estimate M. What happens to M if λ is halved?
quiz.a: M ≈ V²/2 = 200. Halving λ doubles V, so M becomes about 800.

quiz.q: Write the single-mode condition in terms of V.
Why does graded-index reduce modal dispersion?
quiz.a: Longer curved rays travel in lower-index glass where light is faster, so arrival times become closer.

quiz.q: Why must n<sub>1</sub> exceed n<sub>2</sub> in both profiles?
quiz.a: Total internal reflection at the core–cladding boundary requires the core to have the higher refractive index.

beyond: Not for the exam. Newer fibres use bend-insensitive profiles, photonic-crystal cladding, few-mode cores and multicore designs to raise capacity. Search 'photonic crystal fibre', 'few-mode fibre' and 'multicore fibre' to continue. The same V-number idea reappears when you check whether a fibre is single-mode.
